items.title: Greenpeace drops nine celebrity-signed boulders to curb North Sea fishing
items.author: TOI WORLD DESK
items.description: Environmental activists from Greenpeace have deployed nine limestone boulders in the Southern North Sea to prevent bottom trawling. This underwater barrier aims to protect marine biodiversity, particularly harbour porpoises affected by industrial fishing. Greenpeace argues that government protections have been insufficient to shield marine habitats from destructive fishing methods. The deployment of boulders took place without a marine licence, raising regulatory concerns.

items.title: Ludhiana girl, 6, holds difficult yoga pose for 18 minutes, sets record
items.author: TOI LIFESTYLE DESK
items.description: At just six years old, Sarah Sangar from Ludhiana has made headlines by holding the seated wide-legged yoga pose on a gymnastics balance beam for 18 minutes and 20 seconds, setting a new record. Recognized by the India Book of Records on October 3, 2026, this accomplishment not only highlights her impressive bodily control and flexibility but also encourages children everywhere to pursue excellence in physical fitness through dedicated training.

items.title: Microsoft says no to UK's most-valuable startup Nscale amid Texas data centre woes
items.author: TOI TECH DESK
items.description: Microsoft has chosen not to extend its deal with Nscale for additional computing capacity in Texas. This decision poses significant challenges for Nscale, which is preparing for a potential IPO. Nscale faces further obstacles as Microsoft previously withdrew from a major deal for its Essex data centre. The company, supported by Nvidia, is also encountering delays with its flagship facility in West Virginia.
